2609.13806.title: Understanding the Limits of Agentic ICD Coding
2609.13806.paper_summary: ICD-10-CM codes are alphanumeric codes used in the US to classify diagnoses and injuries for medical billing and epidemiological reporting. Standard ICD-10-CM benchmarks report aggregate metrics that obscure performance on complex coding scenarios. We evaluate neural, workflow, and agentic systems on a rarity-stratified set of MIMIC-IV discharge summaries and identify two orthogonal failure modes. Neural classifiers exhibit a 0.43 micro-F1 gap between rare and common codes. Workflow systems handle rare codes well but score near zero on injury and external cause codes that require multi-step guideline following. A tool-augmented agentic configuration with structured access to official ICD-10-CM reference materials recovers up to 0.34 micro-F1 on this subset. No single system dominates across all conditions.
2609.13806.paper_summary_zh: ICD-10-CM 代碼是用於美國的字母數字代碼，用於對診斷和傷害進行分類，以便於醫療計費和流行病學報告。標準的 ICD-10-CM 基準報告聚合指標，掩蓋了在複雜編碼場景中的表現。我們在一組根據稀有性分層的 MIMIC-IV 出院摘要上評估神經、工作流程和代理系統，並識別出兩種正交失效模式。神經分類器在稀有代碼和常見代碼之間顯示出 0.43 的微 F1 差距。工作流程系統對稀有代碼處理良好，但在需要多步驟指導的傷害和外部原因代碼上得分接近零。一個增強工具的代理配置，對官方 ICD-10-CM 參考材料進行結構化訪問，能在這個子集上恢復高達 0.34 的微 F1。沒有任何單一系統在所有條件下佔據主導地位。
